correctness.rationale: The finite graph is specified by all 24 edges. Two independent exact acyclicity tests agree on all 65,536 masks, yielding 50,996 nonempty faces. The matching has 25,475 pairs; every one of 375,040 directed Hasse cover relations is included in a complete topological-sort acyclicity check. Signed gradient path projection supplies the integral 8×33 B9 and zero 33×4 B10. The explicit 8×8 determinant -1 minor proves B9 onto over Z and H9=Z^25, H10=Z^4. The Morse CW model has no cells in dimensions 1 through 7, and π8(wedge S8) and π9(wedge S9) are the corresponding free abelian degree groups, so the unimodular elementary cancellations and zero remaining degree vectors prove the claimed homotopy wedge, not just homology. All code/output embedded are from this graph and replayable.

value.rationale: Vertex-induced forests form a natural simplicial feasibility complex for feedback-vertex sets and decycling. The Möbius–Kantor graph is a canonical sixteen-vertex cubic symmetric non-cactus incidence graph, outside the primary published classes of the forest filtration. An explicit integral homotopy identification involving two adjacent sphere dimensions (25 in degree 9, four in degree 10) is a natural nontrivial complete classification and reproducibility benchmark. The mixed attaching-map calculation is mathematically necessary and adds more than basic counts, homology ranks, or a special-case routine identity.
